item.title: Star RB Fluff Bothwell returning to Mississippi in 2027 with Kamario Taylor
item.description: Wesley Hale-Imagn Images Star RB Fluff Bothwell returning to Mississippi in 2027 with Kamario Taylor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mississippi State had an amazing start to the season. They opened up 4-0, which included wins over Minnesota, South Carolina, and Missouri. Then, the injuries started to pile up. Star quarterback Kamario Taylor was lost for the season, and running back Fluff Bothwell also missed time. As the team sits at 4-6, plans are already being made for the 2027 campaign. Taylor has already comitted to returning to the Bulldogs next year. Now, Bothwell has decided to join him , according to a statement released by the running back through the school on social media. “Choosing Mississippi State was the best decision I’ve ever made. I came here to play in the best offensive scheme in college football – a running back’s dream. I also came to grow as a player and as a man, and to represent the maroon and white like all the greats before us. That’s why, every day, I’m going to keep fighting for Mississippi State alongside my coaches and teammates to make the entire Bulldog Family proud. Thanks to Coach Lebby and Coach Tucker for believing in me! I’m ALL IN on this program. We’re focused on these last two games, then going straight to work on a big 2027. Hail State!” the statement read. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bothwell was lightly recruited in the class of 2024. He was a three-star recruit, sitting at the 127th running back in the class. This led to his commitment to South Alabama. He broke out immediately in 2024, running for 832 yards and 13 touchdowns. Bothwell then hit the transfer portal and joined Mississippi State last season. In his first season with the Bulldogs, he ran for 677 yards and six touchdowns. This year, he has run for 649 yards and three scores, while also having 157 yards receiving and a touchdown. This is while dealing with injuries. He ran the ball just one time against Alabama before being hurt, and then missed the next game. It is of note the thank you to Jeff Lebby. The Mississippi State coach is in his third season as the head coach. The six-game skid for the Bulldogs, along with the fact that they could miss a bowl, has led to speculation that Lebby is on the hot seat at Mississippi State . With both Taylor and Bothwell committing to 2027, and Bothwell specifically calling out Lebby, the university may be keeping the coach to keep the players. item.title: ‘Ya’ll know the price’: Floyd Schofield Sr calls out Abdullah Mason’s team over ‘lowball offer’
item.description: There’s been some initial talks of a potential meeting between Floyd ‘Kid Austin’ Schofield and Abdullah Mason but it would seem things aren’t going so smoothly as the sides are apparently far apart on the money. During a recent social media post Schofield’s father, Floyd Schofield Sr , would call out Mason’s team for what they say was an insulting offer for the fight. “How ya’ll going to send us a lowball offer,” Schofield Sr would say. “Isn’t that some bullsh-t. That is so Mason. Anyway, ya’ll know we ain’t taking no $700,000. Come on, now. Ya’ll know the offer is $2.5M, that’s the offer, period. That’s it. Make that happen so we can fight. All this ‘we’ll give you a million, you bring home $700,000’, nah. Ya’ll know the price. “We ain’t even going to fool the fans. Either ya’ll ready to fight or ya’ll had a purse to fight or ya’ll don’t and we go on to Rayo [Valenzuela] and we do what we got to do. Don’t waste our time with no bull crap offers. $2.5M at least, and that’s it. Ya’ll already knew that before you sent that bogus offer.” Based strictly on what Sr says here, they are seeking more than twice the amount of money than has been offered thus far, and that would appear to be a wide gulf to bridge considering the actual economics of a matchup of this kind, considering neither fighter is a particularly huge draw. That being the case, this proposed fight could be dead in the water in the early going.

It is a perfectly good fight against a decent, proven opponent, but Price has her sights set firmly on one of the sport’s big names. During the last year, various boxers have been linked with Price; deals have been reached, with fights close to being made, and then the contests have collapsed. It is not unusual, but it is frustrating. In theory, there is still an active plan to fight the world’s No 1 female fighter Claressa Shields in America. Shields is unbeaten in 19 fights, has won world titles at four different weights, and is desperate for a test. item.title: TT 2027 Sidecar regulations amended
item.description: TT organisers say they recognise the changes may mean a "smaller field" next year [BBC] New rules for the Sidecar class at TT 2027 have dropped requirements for the likes of bodywork, fairings and aerodynamics, but teams are still required to switch to Sportbike engines and electronic control systems. The rules, implemented following a review of the future of sidecars at the races, were revised after feedback from competitors and teams about the cost and time available to make the necessary changes. In June, the class was suspended on safety grounds. Rules introduced last week led to the withdrawal of three teams and prompted race organisers to review their plans. On Wednesday, the racing body said the new measures which have now been decided upon were central to delivering "the significant and controllable" reduction in speed which was required for the return of the class for 2027 and beyond. "We recognise from the outset the time, investment and practical undertaking required of competitors and teams to adapt to the new regulations - and that initially the field will be smaller," organisers said. The effectiveness of the changes would be reviewed during and after TT 2027, they added, "taking account of incident evidence, speeds and machinery performance, technical compliance and reliability, competitor feedback, specialist technical input and the amount of qualifying and racing completed". Organisers said the class had an "established place" in the history of the event and "the responsibility now is to make changes, and create the conditions so it can continue and develop over the longer term". Two races are confirmed to take place around the Mountain Course in June next year. item.title: Hammered: Worst Duke Losses Since 2020
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 17: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils reacts after fouling out in the second half against the Illinois Fighting Illini during their game at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 17, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images W hen things didn’t go well for Duke against Illinois the other night, the 99-78 loss at Iconic Cameron Indoor Stadium (“iconic” is de rigueur nowadays) was a bit of a shock. Jon Scheyer ’s talent rich Blue Devils don’t lose often, especially not at home. Duke usually ranks high in the polls, sometimes the only ACC team that’s sufficiently strong to merit national attention. When and if Duke loses we expect the action to be intense, the score to be close. The game against the Illini wasn’t close. Losing by only a few points feels different than falling by a double figure margin, which implies the victor was clearly dominant, even if only at game’s end. Under first Mike Krzyzewski and, most recently, Scheyer, the Devils have fallen by 11 points or more just 13 times in this decade, that is the 2019-20 season through Nov. 17, 2026. Last season Duke lost only three games – against Texas Tech at Madison Square Garden in December, at UNC in early February, and by a point against UConn in the Elite Eight. The three ’26 defeats were by a combined five points, making the size of the early Illinois defeat rather unexpected. The 21-point losing margin against the Illini was exceeded only three times since 2020. In fact, and here’s a real oddity, under former head coach Kevin Keatts NC State delivered more of Duke’s most decisive defeats than anyone else over the course of the last six-plus seasons. That includes the largest margin, 84-60 at Raleigh in 2023, and a stinging ejection from the 2024 NCAA Tournament. Illinois has twice decisively outmuscled the Blue Devils, in the early 2022 season and again in this one, both times under Brad Underwood. UNC also twice won against Duke by comfortable margins, in 2021 and 2022, under Hubert Davis. item.title: Veteran righty pitches lights-out despite injury-plagued 2026
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Nick Pivetta #27 of the San Diego Padres pitches in the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game three of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on October 06, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Nick Pivetta When the Padres signed Pivetta heading into the 2025 season, he was the last solid starting pitcher left on the free agent market. No other reliable options remained. San Diego signed him to a backloaded deal in order to maintain payroll flexibility. Pivetta turned in the best season of his career, earning some down-ballot Cy Young votes. He was expected to anchor the rotation alongside Michael King in 2026. Overall Grade: C- Things didn’t go according to plan. Pivetta made just four starts before hitting the injured list and remaining there for almost five months. He exited a start against the Colorado Rockies early and was later diagnosed with flexor strain in his throwing elbow. He ended up making just eight starts in total for the Friars due to several setbacks during his rehab assignments. But, when he was on the mound, it was a thing of beauty. Pivetta pitched to a 2.86 ERA in those eight starts (34.2 IP). He was even better after returning from the IL, posting a 1.45 ERA in the month of September. His overall ERA was only so high due to a rough Opening Day performance (6 ER, 3.0 IP). Removing that first outing, Pivetta holds a 1.42 ERA across 31 2/3 innings of work. He just didn’t pitch enough. The injury concerns led the Padres to decline his $14 million club option for the 2027 season. Reportedly, the two sides are still seeking a reunion. Had the Friars picked up Pivetta’s 2027 club option, he would have acquired an $18 million player option for 2028. San Diego probably didn’t want to be on the hook for that much if Pivetta’s arm gave out a second year in a row.

item.title: Cardinals’ Carson Beck Makes Notable Admission About His First NFL Start
item.description: Carson Beck finally got a taste of what it’s like to start a game in the pros after the Arizona Cardinals handed the rookie the keys to the offense in Week 10 against the Los Angeles Rams. Although Beck didn’t exactly shine in the Rams game, he had great things to say about the lead-up to that assignment against Myles Garrett and company. “I think that routine really helped and to be quite honest, like that was the most prepared I’ve ever felt for a football game in my life ever,” the former Miami Hurricanes star quarterback said talking to reporters on Wednesday. “So, it definitely helps that, you know, you’re able to be at the facility for, twelve, thirteen hours a day. But man, that’s that definitely props to, my coaches and, you know, how much time they spent just getting me ready and prepared for the game.” "To be quite honest, that's the most prepared I've ever felt for a football game in my life…ever." Carson Beck is confident in his coaches and preparation. pic.twitter.com/CQL0CqGMYy — PHNX Cardinals (@PHNX_Cardinals) November 18, 2026 Cardinals Rookie Beck Inherits QB1 Role Amid Interesting Turn of Events at Quarterback Nov 15, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck (19) warms up before the game against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images Beck becomes the Cardinals’ starting quarterback not entirely by design but partly out of necessity. Arizona started the season with Jacoby Brissett as its QB1. Several weeks later, he was replaced in favor of Gardner Minshew. Brissett was then traded to the Baltimore Ravens and Minshew is now done for the remainder of the season with an injury. That opened the door for Beck to take over the QB1 role for perhaps at least the rest of the campaign. Against the Rams, Beck went 11/18 for 108 passing yards and zero touchdowns. He was picked off twice and got sacked five times for a loss of 19 yards. It was quite a tough day for Beck, but he can get better with more reps. Beck will get another chance to impress on Sunday, albeit against another quality team in the form of the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City. item.title: Barcelona superstar intent on reclaiming his place in Hansi Flick’s starting XI
item.description: Barcelona superstar intent on reclaiming his place in Hansi Flick’s starting XI Frenkie de Jong’s return from injury, although quite late, has served as a reminder for Barcelona as to why he is such a key player for the club. De Jong’s versatility has helped Barcelona navigate through an apparent injury crisis before the international break. This is despite the fact that De Jong was almost counted out by many, when Barça signed Rodri from Manchester City in the summer. De Jong ready to reclaim his place According to AS , De Jong is now prepared to go a step further and reclaim his regular starting role in the Barcelona first-team, as the club look to resume their campaign this weekend. De Jong has shown a lot of positivity since returning from injury. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As mentioned earlier, de Jong has already shown his commitment towards the team by playing in various roles, including as a right-back against Atletico Madrid and as a central defender against Alaves. He also played as an attacking midfielder against Real Madrid. Such kind of commitment came on the back of an ugly summer that saw him pick up an injury and returning to full fitness much later than initially expected. De Jong grew frustrated with his standing in the team during that time. But he is not keen on making a big fuss out of his situation and is ready to fight for his place in the team, in any way he can. That is part of the reason why the former Ajax sensation accepted the role of a right-back when Hansi Flick decided to start Marc Bernal in central midfield against Atletico Madrid. De Jong winning back the trust Can de Jong regain his place in the Barcelona starting eleven? (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) De Jong’s positive attitude hasn’t gone unnoticed by Barcleona fans, at the very least. His standing in the dressing room also remains high, with the midfielder even receiving praise from the new Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez, who had given him the captaincy in the absence of Virgil van Dijk in the international break. While De Jong’s relationship with fans remains a love-hate affair, he was warmly received both against Alaves and on reaching 300 appearances for the club. De Jong remains strong and motivated, as he stated recently. He also rubbished claims of him refusing to play in last season’s UCL quarter-final against Atletico Madrid. Perhaps more importantly, his resurgence has led to calls of him starting together with Rodri and Pedri in midfield, though the chances of that remain slim. For now, De Jong will be focusing on getting back to full fitness for the Villarreal clash, though he has already received the green light to feature in that game.

item.title: Tyler Herro confirms what his relationship with Bam Adebayo is really like
item.description: Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tyler Herro hasn’t spoken to Bam Adebayo ahead of tonight’s matchup. Miami beat Milwaukee 137–130 on Wednesday night, and Bam Adebayo definitely got the upper hand on his old teammate. Adebayo put up 26 points, four rebounds, and two assists, while Tyler Herro had a rough night back in South Beach with just eight points and four assists on 4-of-11 shooting. Their seven-year run in Miami ended on ugly terms this past summer after Herro got shipped to the Bucks in the blockbuster Giannis Antetokounmpo trade. Leaked screenshots from an alleged burner account showed Herro trashing Adebayo’s contract and game, sparking a reported fight in Las Vegas, and the two didn’t interact once on Wednesday. Tyler Herro admits him and Bam Adebayo haven’t spoken Before tip-off against the Heat on Wednesday night, reporters asked Tyler Herro where things actually stand with Bam Adebayo after their messy summer fallout. His response: “I’m not sure. I mean, I haven’t talked to him. Obviously, spent a lot of time with Bam. I admire his game. He’s a great player. Can do everything on the floor. Guard one through five. Obviously, he’s gifted offensively, but I know how he’s wired. I know he’s a competitor, and I know how it’s going to be tonight, so I’m excited to just go up against everybody.” Tyler Herro and Bam Adebayo barely acknowledged each other all night. item.description: The Premier League has revealed the kick-off times and TV schedule for its remaining January fixtures, with a number of huge match-ups moved into prime-time slots. Liverpool host Manchester United in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as United boss this weekend and the reverse fixture between the two bitter rivals takes place in matchweek 22, with the game being moved into the Sky Sports slot at 4.30pm on Sunday 24 January. Earlier that day will have seen a London derby between Crystal Palace and Tottenham as one of four 2pm fixtures, while the previous day (Saturday 23 January) is headlined by Brighton vs Manchester City at 8pm on TNT Sports , with reigning champions Arsenal facing Newcastle at 5.30pm on Sky Sports that day. Meanwhile matchweek 21 sees the rare occurrence of Arsenal, Man City, Liverpool and Chelsea all playing at 3pm on a Saturday (16 January) with Hull, Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Sunderland the respective opponents. item.title: Woods to design new golf course in Northern Ireland
item.description: Woods said the new course is a special opportunity for his design firm [Getty Images] Tiger Woods is to design Northern Ireland's first new championship links golf course in more than a century. On Thursday, Woods and his course architecture firm TGR Design unveiled plans for Bellarena Golf Links on the Causeway Coast. The course will be located on Northern Ireland's northwest coast, about 20 miles west of three-time Open Championship venue Royal Portrush. Fifteen-time major champion Woods said the opportunity to create a new course in one of golf's most celebrated destinations was a special one. "Northern Ireland is home to some of the greatest links golf in the world, and building one on the Causeway Coast is a special opportunity for our team," said Woods. "We want Bellarena to feel as though it has always been part of this coastline, with a course that challenges the best players and is fun for everyone who plays it." The development, a partnership between Galgorm Collection and US-based Reef Destinations, is expected to break ground in 2027, subject to planning approval, with a target opening date of July 2029. "To have Tiger Woods and his company design a golf course in Northern Ireland is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, it's unbelievable," said Galgorm Collection chief executive Colin Johnston. "It's bringing together fantastic companies and partners and creating something that will benefit Northern Ireland for many years to come." Johnston said the dramatic setting was one of the key reasons the site stood out. "The backdrop of Binevenagh Mountain and the views over Lough Foyle and into the Donegal hills are just stunning," he said. The project could provide a boost to tourism in the north west. "We know golf tourism is huge and we know it's close to capacity," Johnston said. "If we want to bring more people to this part of the world, we need to increase that capacity, and it needs to be at the elite level people expect when they come here." Johnston believes Bellarena can complement Northern Ireland's world-renowned venues such as Royal Portrush and Royal County Down by helping attract new visitors. "This is about bringing something new and exciting to this part of the world, bringing more people here and increasing tourism overall," he added. Unlike some exclusive championship venues, Bellarena is expected to operate as a non-member, pay-and-play course. TGR has designed courses in the United States but Bellarena will be the firm's first project in Europe. Woods set to return next month after two years out

The Philadelphia 76ers have gotten off to a red-hot start to the season, posting a 13-3 record that sees them sit at the top of the Eastern Conference standings. This shouldn't come as too much of a surprise, given that all of their top talents have been firing on all cylinders, with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown all averaging 20 points or more. But Wednesday night's win over the Orlando Magic saw them overcome a new challenge in the season: a stacked injury report. Philadelphia was without the aforementioned Maxey and Brown, which could cause some concern for the Sixers faithful, but for Maxey, there isn't much to worry about. Nick Nurse said Tyrese Maxey and Dean Wade were held out mostly out of precaution. Maxey went through shootaround this morning, but his foot began bothering him pregame. Just wanted to hold him out for this one. #Sixers — Ky Carlin (@Ky_Carlin) November 19, 2026 According to USA Today's Ky Carlin, the Sixers' coach stated that the two-time All-Star was held out of the match just as a precaution. Brown to undergo further tests However, according to Carlin , the prognosis for Brown's hamstring strain that kept him out of Wednesday night's match will have to wait a little longer, as the team will re-evaluate him when they return from their road trip. "He’s gonna get re-evaluated when we get back home," Carlin wrote, quoting the aforementioned Nurse. "So. just know he's out tonight and we'll look at him when we get back." Given that Philadelphia has two days off ahead of their NBA Cup match against the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday night, all eyes will be on the results of the tests for Brown's injury. The five-time All-Star has been one of the more lethal parts of Philadelphia's offensive arsenal, averaging 22.6 points and 6.6 rebounds per night, while shooting 49.4 percent from the field. item.description: ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. – For years, longtime Sea Island instructor Jack Lumpkin carried around a list of places where he believed the Seaside Course could be lengthened. “Whenever anybody would listen, he'd take us out there and show us, ‘You should back this tee up,’” Davis Love III recalled. Lumpkin passed away several years ago, but his vision has finally become reality. Ahead of this week's RSM Classic, Sea Island unveiled a multi-million-dollar restoration of its famed Seaside Course led by Love Golf Design, headed by Love, his brother, Mark, and lead architect Scott Sherman, in collaboration with MacCurrach Golf Construction. The project was designed to honor the course's architectural heritage while enhancing playability for resort guests and adding subtle challenge for tournament competitors. Originally designed by Harry Colt and Charles Alison in 1929, the Seaside Course underwent a major renovation in 1999 when Tom Fazio combined nine holes from the original Alison layout and nine from a Joe Lee-designed course to create an entirely new 18-hole design. The latest restoration included a complete turf replacement, infrastructure upgrades, dune restoration and a series of strategic refinements throughout the property. “We used historic pictures and Google Earth as a guide to restore Tom Fazio's original vision,” Love said. Among the changes are new back tees on Nos. 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 and 16, adding roughly 150 yards to the par-70 layout, which now stretches to 7,157 yards. Many of those additions trace directly to suggestions Lumpkin championed for years. The project also included installation of a new irrigation system. The greens remain TifEagle Bermudagrass, while the collars, approaches, tees, fairways and rough were converted to Platinum Paspalum, a grass variety prized for its salt tolerance in coastal environments. item.title: Emi Martinez backs Como star Nico Paz to take over Lionel Messi’s iconic Argentina No. 10 jersey
item.description: Argentina v Costa Rica - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez believes Como standout Nico Paz has the potential to inherit Lionel Messi's iconic No. 10 shirt for Argentina. The young midfielder recently scored a brace against Costa Rica, sparking intense debate about his future international role. Martinez backs Paz for iconic shirt Martinez believes Paz has the quality to become Argentina's next No. 10. The debate over who will inherit the legendary jersey has intensified following Messi's international retirement . Paz thrust himself into the spotlight on Tuesday by scoring a brace in Argentina's emphatic 7-0 victory over Costa Rica . The Como midfielder has now registered a remarkable five goals in his last five appearances for the national team. His rapid emergence has made him a highly credible candidate to step into the playmaking void. Senior players within the Argentina setup are already throwing their support behind the youngster. Building the Argentine fighting spirit Martinez, a key figure in the Argentina dressing room, has expressed immense confidence in the midfielder's potential. The goalkeeper revealed that the squad is actively nurturing the Como star to prepare him for the biggest stages. "I see him becoming more and more integrated into the group," the Chelsea player admitted, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo . "Obviously, he needs to have that Argentine fighting spirit, and we’re helping him develop it. The truth is, he deserves everything that’s happening to him right now. He deserves to be here and to play. The goals he’s scoring are an added bonus." Embracing the ultimate national responsibility Taking over the primary creative role for Argentina comes with immense pressure, but Martinez feels Paz possesses the correct mindset. The veteran believes humility will be the defining factor in the youngster's long-term success. "If he maintains this humility and keeps performing at this level, Nico Paz can definitely wear Argentina’s No. 10 shirt and take on that responsibility," Martinez added. "We need players like him, players who see themselves as leaders. He can help us win a lot of games. We have to help him. We’re a national team. There are no egos here. It’s all about hard work, humility, and respect." Shining bright in Italy and beyond Paz is currently enjoying a remarkable rise at club level, having just started his third season with Como. During the previous campaign, he was instrumental in helping Cesc Fabregas' team secure Champions League qualification for the first time in their history. That impressive form has seamlessly carried over into the 2026-27 season. The dynamic midfielder has already racked up six goals and eight assists in just 14 appearances across all competitions for the Italian club.

item.title: Hamilton picks Verstappen as target for hilarious cheese bazooka attack
item.description: Lewis Hamilton has jokingly named Max Verstappen as the Formula 1 driver he would target with a giant cheese bazooka, following an unusual question from fans during an event in Las Vegas. While the media have been asking drivers more serious questions about their performances, the championship battle and the challenges awaiting them at the Las Vegas Grand Prix , fans have taken a rather different approach, putting Hamilton on the spot with a particularly bizarre question. The seven-time world champion was taking part in a fan event ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix when he was presented with a rather unconventional scenario involving a hypothetical weapon fitted to his Ferrari steering wheel. Asked which driver he would shoot if he had a button capable of firing melted cheese from a giant bazooka, Hamilton initially struggled to settle on a name. "That's a really good question. Who should I blast with cheese? That's pretty funny," the Ferrari driver responded. After someone suggested that a particular driver was already on his mind, Hamilton insisted he was still undecided and turned to the audience for suggestions. "No, I don't know who to pick. Who do you all think would be good?" Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Hamilton rules out Leclerc before settling on Verstappen Verstappen was the first name suggested by the crowd, prompting an amused reaction from Hamilton. "Verstappen?" he repeated, laughing, before asking: "Anyone else?" Another fan proposed Charles Leclerc, but Hamilton immediately ruled out targeting his Ferrari teammate, explaining that their shared responsibilities on the track should take priority. "He's my teammate. I can't say my teammate. We have to win as a team," Hamilton replied. The Briton then floated Lando Norris as another possible target, before someone in the audience suggested Nico Hulkenberg. However, Hamilton was unwilling to pick the German, describing him as harmless. "Nico's harmless. Everyone's saying Max, so maybe I'll go with that. He's probably the closest, so let's cover Max in cheese."

item.description: 2 Newcastle players ruled out of Arsenal clash Newcastle United will be without a couple of players for Arsenal’s visit on Saturday, but the vast majority of their players are expected to be fit. Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images Newcastle United are expected to have one significant injury absentee for Arsenal’s visit to St. James’ Park this weekend, with Joelinton set to miss the match. Joelinton missed Newcastle’s last game against Fulham with a thigh issue,, and there was some initial uncertainty around exactly how long he’d be out. But Lee Ryder confirms for The Journal that the player has at least been ruled out of the Arsenal fixture. Newcastle will also be without backup goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen , but that’s unlikely to have a material impact on the result. The 20-year-old is still waiting on his Premier League debut. Photo by Ed Sykes/Getty Images Then former Arsenal player Joe Willock and ex-Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez were both missing from training earlier this week due to illness, but the duo are expected to return in time for the weekend fixture. So in terms of potential starters, Joelinton is the only player who won’t be available to Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle . Arsenal are obviously in a relatively similar situation, with Bukayo Saka the only confirmed injury absentee for the match. But Max Dowman will also be missing through the final game of his suspension, Martin Zubimendi is a doubt, and William Saliba is still yet to play any first-team minutes after injury. Talking trade We start with the trade inside the top five, with the New York Jets moving up to No. 2 to draft Drew Mestemaker from Oklahoma State. There are a few things to discuss when it comes to this hypothetical. The Jets are loaded with three picks in the first round, but if they want to draft the quarterback at the top of their board, they will likely have to move ahead of the Miami Dolphins at No. 3. With picks No. 4 and No. 13, they can do just that, while retaining a pick at No. 6 (courtesy of the Indianapolis Colts and the Sauce Gardner trade) to address another position of need. In this scenario that is Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore. But … trading up for a quarterback prospect who did not even start for his high school team and is just in his first year as a starter for a Power 4 school? There is a lot to like about Mestemaker, from his ability in the downfield passing game, his athleticism, his willingness to challenge tough windows over the middle, and his touch when layering throws to all levels of the field. But in many ways it is that fact, that he is wrapping up his first year as a starter at a Power 4 school, that works in his favor. The trajectory is impressive and the upside is off the charts. I was a fan of his after last year , and have only grown more impressed with his profile. As for the Chargers’ side of this trade, they get a new target for Justin Herbert in Charlie Becker out of Indiana, and Ashton Hampton to address a need in the secondary. Where is Arch Manning? This is likely the next big question: Where is Arch Manning? Sitting here on the cusp of Thanksgiving, I’m not sure Manning enters the draft. His game against LSU — much like his games against Ole Miss and Ohio State earlier this season — was another microcosm of his current draft profile: Some great moments late, overshadowing some difficult moments earlier. Now, maybe Manning does enter the draft, and if he does it will be interesting to see how the greater draft community stacks him with the rest of this class. But right now, I think it is more likely he heads back to Texas, or even entertains the transfer portal, than he heads to the NFL. What about the rest of the quarterbacks? Now let’s talk about the rest of the quarterbacks … both those listed here and two names that are not. We can start with the two quarterbacks not listed here in this first-round mock: Austin Simmons and Trinidad Chambliss. Beginning with Simmons, much like Manning I think he heads back to Missouri for another season. Simmons recently signed a new deal with the school for 2027 , but he does have an option to enter the NFL Draft. But with the Tigers’ recent slide, I think it is likely he heads back to campus with that new deal in hand, to try and make another run. As for Chambliss, as much as I like him, I do wonder if the NFL will view him the same way that I do. He might slide to the top of the second round, which will not be a bad thing for him. That leaves Dante Moore as the next quarterback off the board, to the Cleveland Browns. While Deshaun Watson has stabilized that position this season, Cleveland still needs a long-term solution, and Moore was a potential top-five pick a year ago, and the talent is there. Then we get CJ Carr to the Minnesota Vikings at the end of the first round. I think he would be a good fit for Kevin O’Connell, and it sets up a scenario where yet again Kirk Cousins could be mentoring a first-round pick. This idea sent me down the road of a “Mandalorian” world where Cousins just mentors a first-round pick to start each season before moving on to a team making a surprise playoff run despite a glaring need at the position. A hired gun, spaghetti Western style, year after year. I’ve said to much. But you know where to find me Netflix. A running back in the top 10? I know, I know … But the more I thought about pairing Jaden Baugh with the Houston Texans, the more sense it made. And one does not need to look far for inspiration. Take the Kansas City Chiefs, who stabilized their running game with the addition of Kenneth Walker III this past offseason. Walker has given Kansas City an explosive element in the run game, and put the Chiefs back among the AFC’s list of elite teams. For a team like the Texans, bolstering the running attack makes a world of sense. While part of it is game-script dependent, Houston ranks 29th in the league in rushing yards per game , and 24th in Expected Points Added per Rush. Going offensive line here is also an option for Houston but Baugh, who is explosive both on the ground and through the air, is a fun fit for them.

item.title: 'I feel like we're in an Orwell novel right now': Joel Klatt slams CFP selection committee
item.description: Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images, The Joel Klatt Show We got another look at the College Football Playoff selection committee’s rankings on Tuesday, and there is once again plenty to talk about . While there were a few eyebrow-raising decisions across the top 25 — four ranked four-loss SEC teams, Arizona moving up four spots with a loss, Indiana at No. 8 after its shuffling last week — the biggest question mark by a pretty wide margin was the committee’s ranking of No. 3 Alabama relative to No. 5 Texas. There was no great move here, as Alabama held serve at No. 3 with a comfortable win over Vanderbilt, while Texas moved up one spot following its on-the-road win over No. 21 LSU. Instead, it was the lack of movement that was the real news. After the Hoosiers got punished during their bye week, presumably as a result of several of their previous wins taking losses while they were off, many expected the same to happen for the Crimson Tide this week, as Alabama’s five best wins this season all lost this past week. Instead, the committee remained unshaken in its faith in Bama. Joel Klatt, who has never been shy about sharing his opinions on the committee’s rankings, did not hold back while breaking down what he saw as an insult to college football fans. “I feel like we’re in an Orwell novel right now,” Klatt said on Wednesday. “The committee is basically insisting we reject the evidence right before our eyes. Right in front of our faces. It is like their most essential command. “I see the resume between Alabama and Texas. Two spots behind Alabama is Texas, and Texas’ resume is so much better than Alabama’s. Their best wins, Bama, are now Kentucky and South Carolina, who just got the hinges blown off of their front door by Arkansas. … Texas beat Tennessee and Ohio State. A Tennessee team that beat Alabama. There’s no comparing those two resumes. You took a wrong turn, you’re telling us it’s a shortcut, and now you’re just stubborn. Take the crayons away from the committee.” Klatt then imagined a conversation he’d have with a defender of the committee’s current ranking, pointing out the circular reasoning of those that argue in favor of the SEC’s ranked four-loss teams. “The Tide looked very average. ‘Yeah, but hey, it was in the SEC.’ Well, why is that good? ‘Well, because nine teams are ranked.’ Yeah, but why were nine teams ranked? ‘Well, because the SEC is really good.’ Why is the SEC really good? ‘Well, because nine teams are ranked.’ Oh! item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on the 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Spurs. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and on to the post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs fans before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under-21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. item.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future

item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling
item.description: Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling. Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days , Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer . He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
item.description: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. item.title: Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come
item.description: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright “With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final . Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. And then England turned up at the Metropolitano . A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would too, but it wasn’t to be. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.content:encoded: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
